checks.description: ISS-0808 regression guard adequacy in tenant_status_test.exs
findings: Test 1 ('a PLATFORM_ADMIN caller (string role) is exempt via roles_from_strings normalization'): calls call_plug(:get, tenant.id, ["PLATFORM_ADMIN"]) against an :inactive tenant; asserts refute conn.halted. If roles_from_strings/1 is removed while @platform_admin remains :PLATFORM_ADMIN, the cond guard becomes :PLATFORM_ADMIN not in ["PLATFORM_ADMIN"] — always true — so the 403 branch fires and conn.halted becomes true, causing refute conn.halted to fail. This test is the definitive regression guard. ✓

Test 2 ('a non-PLATFORM_ADMIN caller is not exempt, even with valid roles'): passes ["PROCESS_OPERATOR"], expects 403. Validates correct non-admin rejection. Note: this test would NOT fail if roles_from_strings/1 were removed (non-admin actors are rejected by both the old and new code paths). It is not a standalone regression guard for the ISS-0808 fix, but it provides valid behavioral coverage.

Test 3 ('an unknown role string is not exempt — roles_from_strings/1 filters out unknown strings'): passes ["PLATFORM_ADMIN_WANNABE"], expects 403. Validates that roles_from_strings/1 correctly drops unrecognized strings (silently returns [] for unknown input, so no atom matches). This guards against future role-string widening. Note: same as test 2, this test passes under a revert of roles_from_strings/1 as long as the atom constant is kept (unknown string never matches the atom); its value is in proving the filter behavior, not the primary regression path.
Conclusion: test 1 alone is a sufficient and mechanically sound regression guard. Tests 2 and 3 add behavioral coverage. The three-test describe block as a whole is fit for purpose.

Pre-existing REQ-075 AC5 tests (the 'PLATFORM_ADMIN exempt' describe blocks) provide further supporting signal — they pass ["PLATFORM_ADMIN"] and assert refute conn.halted, so they would also fail under the regression scenario.
